_note: One primary mapping per standard per family. ISO control ids and titles follow the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A structure. PCI DSS requirement numbers are v4.0.x; items marked 'to be verified' were not confirmed against the standard text. GDPR article numbers were not re-checked against the regulation text.

families.label: SMB signing not required
families.rationale: Unsigned SMB sessions allow relay and tampering on the flat hotel LAN, so network and configuration hardening is the control gap.

families.label: LLMNR enabled
families.rationale: Link local name resolution is an unneeded default function that enables credential capture, so it belongs in the hardening baseline.

families.label: Untrusted, self signed, weak or expired certificates
patterns: ^SSL Certificate Signed Using Weak Hashing Algorithm$
families.rationale: Certificates that clients cannot trust defeat the purpose of encryption and train staff to accept warnings; key and certificate management is the gap.

families.label: Legacy TLS and SSL (TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, SSLv2, SSLv3)
families.rationale: Deprecated protocol versions weaken the transport protection of guest and payment related data.

families.label: SWEET32, RC4 and weak key exchange ciphers
families.rationale: 3DES, RC4 and short Diffie-Hellman groups do not meet current strong cryptography expectations.

families.label: Remote access tools (remote control agents, VNC, RDP exposure)
families.rationale: Several overlapping remote tools widen the attack surface; remote access needs one controlled, authenticated and logged path.

families.label: RDP without Network Level Authentication
families.rationale: Without NLA a session is offered before the user authenticates, which weakens secure logon and invites brute force.

families.label: MSMQ QueueJumper and missing patches
families.rationale: A critical remote code execution flaw with a vendor fix shows patches are not applied within a defined time.

families.label: Unsupported or outdated software
families.rationale: Software past vendor support or far behind current versions has no reliable security fixes, so lifecycle tracking is the gap.
families.iso_title: Installation of software on operational systems

families.label: Cleartext and insecure legacy protocols (FTP, SMTP, POP, IMAP, TFTP, NFS, rsync, SMBv1)
families.rationale: Guest and business data moved over cleartext or legacy services can be read or altered in transit; secure transfer rules are missing.

families.label: Legacy simple services and unneeded network responses
families.rationale: Echo, chargen, QOTD and finger have no business use on a hotel server; secure by default configuration removes them.

families.label: SSH weakness (weak ciphers, MACs, Terrapin, password logon)
families.rationale: Weak SSH algorithms and password logon on an administrative channel fall short of strong cryptography for remote administration.
